classification.difficultyReason: The student must replace the coin by its centre, identify the clearance needed from each line, and use the complement of a central safe square to handle overlapping grid-line events.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A coin with a 2 cm diameter is dropped onto a floor ruled by parallel lines that are 3 cm apart. Assume that the floor extends forever in all directions. What is the probability that the coin will land on a line?

spec.sourceRegion: Top of the right column, above part (b); continuation figure for part (a).
spec.description: Seven equally spaced vertical strips and an orange circular coin. The outer rectangle represents an illustrative crop, not a finite floor boundary. House proportions show the stated coin diameter relative to the line spacing; the original coin scale is schematic.
spec.mathematics: Parallel lines are 3 cm apart and the coin has radius 1 cm. No dimension labels are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied coin and floor lines remain visible; no favourable region or answer is shown.

answer.worked:
The coin has radius 1 cm. It touches or crosses a line when its centre is within 1 cm of that line. In a strip 3 cm wide, these two edge regions have total width 2 cm.
$$\begin{align*}\Pr(\text{lands on a line})&=\frac{1+1}{3}\\\Pr(\text{lands on a line})&=\frac{2}{3}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A coin with a 2 cm diameter is dropped onto a grid of squares of side length 3 cm, extending forever in all directions. What is the probability that the coin will land on a line?

spec.description: Seven rows and seven columns of square cells, with an orange circular coin near a vertical line in the lower-left region. The outer boundary represents a crop of the infinite grid. House proportions show the stated coin diameter relative to the cell side; the original coin scale is schematic.
spec.mathematics: Two perpendicular families of lines form squares of side 3 cm. The coin has radius 1 cm. No dimension labels are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied coin and grid remain visible; no safe region or answer is shown.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{8}{9}$

The centre must lie in the central $1\text{ cm}\times1\text{ cm}$ square to avoid every line.
answer.worked:
To avoid every grid line, the coin's centre must be at least 1 cm from each side of a grid square. The safe region is therefore a square of side $3-2=1$ cm. Probability is proportional to area.
$$\begin{align*}\Pr(\text{avoids every line})&=\frac{(3-2)^2}{3^2}\\\Pr(\text{avoids every line})&=\frac{1}{9}\\\Pr(\text{lands on a line})&=1-\frac{1}{9}\\\Pr(\text{lands on a line})&=\frac{8}{9}.\end{align*}$$
